q1_issues.issue: Plural 'herds' is collapsed into a single herd witness, so the sentence's multiple herds - and the distribution of 'large' over them - are lost.
The demonstrative plural subject gets a group-only possession event with no per-member distribution rule, which the instruction set reserves for collective predicates (gather/meet/assemble).

q2_gaps: capitalized ethnonym/demonym used as a common count noun ('these Tuareg') - the proper-noun Name rule vs. a lowercase kind symbol is not resolved
plural collective noun with an of-complement ('herds of cows') - only the singular 'a flock of birds' shape is given, none for a plural group whose members are themselves groups
notes: Holder/Theme on 'have', the demonstrative-plural group witness, and leaving 'large' unfused as a descriptive modifier are all correct. Whether stative 'have' counts as a distributive predicate here is genuinely borderline.
